subject: Deployment mode selection — hosted vs dedicated vs private (post-demo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@fintechco.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode follow-up: hosted vs dedicated vs private

Hi Amanda / Raj,

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from the call and proposed next steps:

- Summary: FintechCo is evaluating options to migrate existing LLM usage from a self-hosted GPU cluster and a legacy API provider. Primary needs are predictable low-latency for customer-facing features, data residency controls, and cost predictability.
- Deployment modes discussed:
  - Hosted API: fastest to integrate, lowest operational overhead, no data residency commitments.
  - Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput, isolation for sensitive workloads.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): full control and KMS integrations for regulated data.

Open questions we need to confirm:
1) Target QPS and peak token throughput.
2) Data residency / regulatory constraints (PII, PCI, etc.).
3) Timeline for migration and whether a dual-run approach is acceptable.

Next steps:
- Please share answers to the three questions above (Raj / procurement contact can reply).
- Would you be open to a 60-minute technical deep-dive with our infra team (we recommend Lauren + Dev) to go over integrated migration options? Proposed slots in related links below.
- Attached is the pricing deck we referenced.

Attachments: redwood_pricing_deck_v3.pdf

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: hosted vs dedicated vs private

Thanks Marissa — great recap.

Short answers:
- Throughput target: 120 QPS average, spikes up to 400 QPS for batch jobs; target p95 latency < 300ms.
- Data: payment card info is tokenized but we have strict residency and audit requirements for user PII.
- Timeline: aiming for production cutover in Q3 2026. We currently run an on-prem GPU cluster and also proxy some traffic to a third-party LLM API for burst traffic.

We are leaning toward Dedicated capacity for latency and isolation, but we want to evaluate Private VPC for certain regulated flows.

Procurement contact is procurement@fintechco.com — looping them for discussing SOW and timelines.

Amanda
Head of ML Platforms
FintechCo
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode follow-up: technical notes for FintechCo

Marissa / Lauren,

Quick technical notes based on Amanda's answers:
- Migration path from on-prem cluster:
  1) Inventory models and tokenizer compatibility. If they use custom fine-tunes, we need model artifacts and a compatibility test run.
  2) KV cache warmup strategy for maintaining low latency during cutover.
  3) Secure key management: KMS/HSM integrations for private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed keys.
  4) Networking: for Private VPC we will need their VPC peering details and firewall rules; for Dedicated we will provide private peering options.
- Risks: peak 400 QPS bursts may require autoscaling/burst capacity planning and batching strategies. We should prepare a cost/latency tradeoff matrix for Dedicated vs Private.

Action items I can take:
- Draft migration checklist and estimated capacity sizing for Dedicated (two sizing options: baseline and peak-ready).
- Prepare list of required artifacts for compatibility tests.

I'll aim to have a draft checklist by Monday. Recommend scheduling the tech deep-dive with Amanda + Raj + procurement and include a short discovery doc in HubSpot.

Thanks,

Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
